metadata.title: The Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent on Generalized Gated Linear Networks
metadata.authors: Samuel Lippl, L.F. Abbott, SueYeon Chung

nodes.name: Gated Linear Network (GLN)
nodes.statement: A deep network where each hidden unit is linear but uses different weights selected by a context function depending on the region of input space, so a unit's output is a context-gated linear function of its input.
nodes.statement_clean: A deep network whose units are linear but pick different weight vectors depending on a context derived from the input region.

nodes.name: Generalized Gated Linear Network
nodes.statement: A class of context-dependent predictors of the form $f_w(x;\gamma):=\langle\mathcal{P}_{\gamma}(w),x\rangle$, where $\gamma\in\Gamma$ indexes a global context and each $\mathcal{P}_{\gamma}$ is a homogeneous polynomial in the global weights $w$.
nodes.statement_clean: Predictors that are linear in $x$ but whose linear coefficients are homogeneous polynomials in the shared weights $w$, with one polynomial per context.

nodes.name: GLN norm
nodes.statement: $\|\beta\|_{\rm GLN}:=\min_{\zeta}\sum_{h=1}^H\|\zeta_h\|_2$ subject to $\beta_{\gamma}=\sum_{h=1}^H\zeta_{h\gamma_h}$, a group-lasso-type norm on the auxiliary variables $\zeta_{h\gamma_h}=w^{(2)}_h w^{(1)}_{h\gamma_h}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A group-lasso-style norm on the context-dependent linear predictors of a two-layer GLN that gradient descent implicitly minimizes.

nodes.name: Frozen-gate ReLU network (FReLU)
nodes.statement: A gated linear network derived from a ReLU network in which the gate sign $\mathrm{sgn}(\langle w,x\rangle)$ that selects between the linear weight $w$ and the zero vector is frozen, and only the linear weights are trained.
nodes.statement_clean: A ReLU network rewritten as a gated linear network whose gates are held fixed during gradient descent.

nodes.name: FReLU norm
nodes.statement: $\|\zeta\|_{\rm FReLU}:=\sum_{h=1}^H\|\zeta_h\|_2$, the group-lasso norm implicitly minimized by gradient descent on FReLUs, where $\beta_{\gamma}=\sum_{h:\gamma_h=1}\zeta_h$.
nodes.statement_clean: A group-lasso norm implicitly minimized by FReLU training.

nodes.name: Exponential-like loss
nodes.statement: A loss $\ell:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ that is monotonically decreasing, differentiable with $\lim_{u\to\infty}\ell(u)=0$, has Lipschitz $\ell'$, and whose $-\ell'$ has a tight exponential tail: $-\ell'(u)$ is sandwiched between $c(1\pm\exp(-\mu_{\pm}u))\exp(-au)$ for large $u$.
nodes.statement_clean: A loss with the exponential's monotonicity, smoothness, and a tight exponential tail on its derivative.

nodes.name: Pair different only in contexts they share
nodes.statement: Two pairs of contexts $(\gamma^{(1)},\gamma^{(2)})$ and $(\tilde{\gamma}^{(1)},\tilde{\gamma}^{(2)})$ that agree on the hidden units where the original pair shares its context, and that copy the original pair on units where it disagrees.
nodes.statement_clean: A pairing notion identifying when two context-pair differences should be equal under the GLN's equivariance.

nodes.name: Support vector
nodes.statement: Data points $S=\{n\mid y^{(n)}\langle\beta,x^{(n)}\rangle=1\}$ for which the margin inequality is tight.
nodes.statement_clean: Training points lying exactly on the maximum-margin separator.

nodes.name: Margin-maximizing linear SVM
nodes.statement: $\min\|\beta\|_2$ s.t. $y^{(n)}\langle\beta,x^{(n)}\rangle\geq 1$, the maximum-margin linear classifier on a linearly separable dataset.
nodes.statement_clean: Find the minimum-norm linear predictor that classifies all training points with margin at least one.

nodes.name: Polynomial-predictor margin problem
nodes.statement: $\min\|w\|_2$ s.t. $y^{(n)}\langle\mathcal{P}(w),x^{(n)}\rangle\geq 1$, the optimization characterizing the asymptotic direction of gradient descent on a deep linear network with homogeneous predictor $\mathcal{P}(w)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Min weight-norm subject to polynomial-margin constraints, the implicit-bias problem for deep linear nets.

nodes.name: Generalized GLN margin problem
nodes.statement: $\min\|w\|_2^2$ s.t. $y^{(n)}f_w(x^{(n)};\gamma^{(n)})\geq 1$, the implicit-bias optimization characterizing the asymptotic direction $\hat{w}$ of gradient descent on a generalized GLN.
nodes.statement_clean: Min weight-norm subject to context-aware margin constraints; the implicit-bias optimization for generalized GLNs.

nodes.name: Equivariance identity for $C=H=2$
nodes.statement: $\beta_{21}-\beta_{22}=\beta_{11}-\beta_{12}$: the difference between two predictors is invariant to the contexts they share.

nodes.name: Two-layer GLN parameterization
nodes.statement: $\beta_{\gamma}=\sum_{h=1}^H w^{(2)}_h w^{(1)}_{h\gamma_h}$, with $w^{(1)}\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times C\times D}$ and $w^{(2)}\in\mathbb{R}^H$.

nodes.name: GLN norm for $C=H=2$
nodes.statement: $\|\beta\|_{\rm GLN}^2=\|\beta\|_2^2+\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}\|\beta_{ij}-\beta_{\overline{i}j}\|_2\|\beta_{ij}-\beta_{i\overline{j}}\|_2$, the closed-form GLN norm in the $C=H=2$ case.

nodes.name: Stationarity for generalized GLN
nodes.statement: $\hat{w}=\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\nabla_w\mathcal{P}_{\gamma}(w)\sum_{n\in S_{\gamma}}\lambda_n y_n x_n$, with $\lambda_n\geq 0$.

nodes.name: Exponential-like loss (Assumption 2)
nodes.statement: $\ell$ is an exponential-like loss in the sense of Definition 1.

nodes.name: Loss tends to zero (Assumption 3)
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{L}(w^{(t)})\to 0$ as $t\to\infty$ along the gradient-descent trajectory.

nodes.name: Direction-convergence of weights (Assumption 4)
nodes.statement: $w^{(t)}$ converges in direction to some unit vector $\hat{w}$.

nodes.name: Positive limiting margin (Assumption 5)
nodes.statement: For all $n$, $y^{(n)}f_{\hat{w}}(x^{(n)};\gamma^{(n)})>0$, excluding pathological cases where the normalized margin still collapses to zero.

nodes.name: Linear-predictor gradient convergence (Assumption 6)
nodes.statement: For each context $\gamma$, $\nabla_{\beta}\mathcal{L}_{\gamma}(\beta_{\gamma}^{(t)})$ converges in direction to some $\hat{z}_{\gamma}$.

nodes.name: Implicit bias of gradient descent on generalized GLNs (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: Under the standing assumptions, if $w^{(t)}$ converges in direction and the loss tends to zero, then the limiting direction $\hat{w}$ is proportional to a stationary point of $\min\|w\|_2^2$ s.t. $y^{(n)}f_w(x^{(n)};\gamma^{(n)})\geq 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Asymptotically, gradient descent on a generalized GLN finds a stationary point of a min-norm problem with context-aware margin constraints.

nodes.name: Soudry et al. SVM convergence (cited)
nodes.statement: For gradient descent on a linearly separable dataset with exponential-like loss, the normalized weight $\hat{\beta}$ converges to the maximum-margin (SVM) direction: a solution of $\min\|\beta\|_2$ s.t. $y^{(n)}\langle\beta,x^{(n)}\rangle\geq 1$.
conclusions: $\hat{\beta}$ is the unit vector of $\arg\min\|\beta\|_2$ s.t. $y^{(n)}\langle\beta,x^{(n)}\rangle\geq 1$

nodes.name: Gunasekar et al. polynomial-predictor convergence (cited)
nodes.statement: For gradient descent on $\langle\mathcal{P}(w),x\rangle$ with $\mathcal{P}$ a homogeneous polynomial of degree $\nu$, if $w^{(t)}$ converges in direction to $\hat{w}$, then $\hat{w}$ is proportional to a stationary point of $\min\|w\|_2$ s.t. $y^{(n)}\langle\mathcal{P}(w),x^{(n)}\rangle\geq 1$.
conclusions: $\hat{w}\propto$ stationary point of the polynomial min-norm problem

nodes.name: Two-layer GLN minimizes the GLN norm
nodes.statement: For a two-layer GLN under Assumptions 2-6, $\hat{\beta}$ is proportional to a minimum of $\|\beta\|_{\rm GLN}$ subject to $y^{(n)}\langle\beta_{\gamma^{(n)}},x^{(n)}\rangle\geq 1$, where $\|\beta\|_{\rm GLN}$ is the group-lasso norm in $\zeta$.
conclusions: $\hat{\beta}\propto\arg\min\|\beta\|_{\rm GLN}$ subject to the unit-margin constraints

nodes.name: Closed form of the GLN norm for $C=H=2$
nodes.statement: For $C=H=2$, $\|\beta\|_{\rm GLN}^2=(\|\beta_{11}-\beta_{12}\|_2+\|\beta_{11}-\beta_{21}\|_2)^2+\|\beta_{12}+\beta_{21}\|_2^2$, equivalently $\|\beta\|_2^2+\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}\|\beta_{ij}-\beta_{\overline{i}j}\|_2\|\beta_{ij}-\beta_{i\overline{j}}\|_2$.
conclusions: $\|\beta\|_{\rm GLN}^2$ admits the explicit two closed forms above

nodes.name: Norm-equivalence formula for $\|\beta\|_2^2$ in $\zeta$ coordinates
nodes.statement: For two-layer GLNs with architectural constraints, $\|\beta\|_2^2=\|A\zeta\|_2^2$ where $(A\zeta)_{hc}=\frac{1}{HC}\sum_{h',c'}\zeta_{h'c'}-\sum_{c'}\zeta_{hc'}+C\zeta_{hc}$.

nodes.name: Equivariance over shared contexts (Lemma 5)
nodes.statement: For any two pairs of contexts $(\gamma^{(1)},\gamma^{(2)})$ and $(\tilde{\gamma}^{(1)},\tilde{\gamma}^{(2)})$ that are different only in contexts they share, $\beta_{\gamma^{(2)}}-\beta_{\gamma^{(1)}}=\beta_{\tilde{\gamma}^{(2)}}-\beta_{\tilde{\gamma}^{(1)}}$.
assumptions: Pair $(\gamma^{(1)},\gamma^{(2)})$ and $(\tilde{\gamma}^{(1)},\tilde{\gamma}^{(2)})$ different only in contexts they share

nodes.name: Architectural degrees of freedom (Lemma 6)
nodes.statement: For a two-layer GLN with $H$ units and $C$ contexts per unit, the linear predictors $\beta_{\gamma}$ for $\gamma\in\overline{\Gamma}$ (contexts where at most one unit's local context differs from 1) can be chosen freely, and they uniquely determine all other $\beta_{\gamma}$; in particular $|\overline{\Gamma}|=(C-1)H+1$.
assumptions: Two-layer GLN with $H$ hidden units, $C$ contexts per unit
conclusions: Exactly $(C-1)H+1$ linear predictors can be chosen freely; the rest follow from the equivariance identity

nodes.name: Extension of Gunasekar's Lemma 8 to exponential-like losses (Lemma 7)
nodes.statement: For almost all linearly separable datasets and exponential-like loss $\ell$, if $\mathcal{L}(\beta^{(t)})\to 0$, $\beta^{(t)}/\|\beta^{(t)}\|_2\to\hat{\beta}$, and $-\nabla_{\beta}\mathcal{L}(\beta^{(t)})/\|\nabla_{\beta}\mathcal{L}(\beta^{(t)})\|_2\to\hat{z}$, then $\hat{z}=\sum_{n\in S_{\mathcal{D}}}\alpha_n y_n x_n$ for some nonnegative $\alpha_n$.
conclusions: $\hat{z}$ is a nonnegative combination of support vectors

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Establish primal feasibility by scaling $\hat{w}$ to satisfy all context-wise margin constraints; establish stationarity by extending the Soudry-Gunasekar arguments contextwise via Lemma 7.

nodes.name: Primal feasibility by context-wise rescaling
nodes.statement: Define $m_{\gamma}:=\min_n y^{(n)}f_{\hat{w}}(x^{(n)};\gamma)$ and scale $w$ by $\alpha:=\max_{\gamma}m_{\gamma}^{-1/\nu_{\gamma}}$ so that $w^{\ast}:=\alpha\hat{w}$ satisfies all margin constraints.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 7 contextwise
nodes.statement: For each $\gamma$, the contextwise loss $\mathcal{L}_{\gamma}(\beta_{\gamma})$ tends to zero and Lemma 7 yields $\hat{z}_{\gamma}=\sum_{n\in S_{\gamma}}\lambda_n y_n x_n$.

nodes.name: Decompose gradient updates by context
nodes.statement: Write $\Delta w^{(t)}_{\gamma}=\eta_t\nabla_w\mathcal{L}_{\gamma}(w)$ and $w^{(t)}=\sum_{\gamma}w^{(t)}_{\gamma}$, splitting the global update into a sum of contextwise pieces.

nodes.name: Express $w^{(t)}_{\gamma}$ via Gunasekar et al. (24)
nodes.statement: Using Gunasekar et al. equation (24), $w^{(t)}_{\gamma}=(\nabla_w\mathcal{P}_{\gamma}(w)\hat{z}+\delta_{\gamma}^{(t)})k_{\gamma}^{(t)}$ where $k_{\gamma}^{(t)}=\sum_{u<t}\eta_u p_{\gamma}(u)g(u)^{\nu_{\gamma}-1}$ and $\delta_{\gamma}^{(t)}\to 0$.

nodes.name: Bounded subsequence of normalized weights
nodes.statement: Define $k^{(t)}=\sum_{\gamma}k_{\gamma}^{(t)}$ and $\hat{k}_{\gamma}^{(t)}=k_{\gamma}^{(t)}/k^{(t)}$. Since $\hat{k}_{\gamma}^{(t)}$ is bounded, extract a convergent subsequence with limit $\hat{k}_{\gamma}$.

nodes.name: Conclude stationarity form
nodes.statement: Take the limit to obtain $\hat{w}\propto\sum_{\gamma}\hat{k}_{\gamma}\nabla_w\mathcal{P}_{\gamma}(\hat{w})\hat{z}$, a nonnegative combination of projected support vectors, proving stationarity.

nodes.name: Proof of GLN-norm characterization (Proposition 8)
nodes.statement: Show that the KKT conditions for the weight-space problem (\ref{eq:th}) and the $\zeta$-space problem (\ref{eq:opt-zeta}) coincide via the change of variables $\zeta_{hc}=w^{(2)}_h w^{(1)}_{hc}$.

nodes.name: Convexity reduction
nodes.statement: Since (\ref{eq:opt-zeta}) is convex (objective convex, constraints linear), it suffices to show $\hat{\zeta}$ is a stationary point.

nodes.name: Forward direction from KKT in $w$
nodes.statement: Use the $w$-KKT condition (\ref{eq:kkt-w}) to derive $\sum_c\|\sum_{\gamma:\gamma_h=c}\phi_{\gamma}\|_2^2=1$ and conclude $\hat{\zeta}_{hc}=\|\hat{\zeta}_h\|_2\sum_{\gamma:\gamma_h=c}\phi_{\gamma}$, satisfying (\ref{eq:kkt-zeta}).

nodes.name: Reverse direction by reconstructing $w$
nodes.statement: Given $\hat{\zeta}$ satisfying (\ref{eq:kkt-zeta}), set $\hat{w}^{(1)}_h=\hat{\zeta}_h/\sqrt{\|\hat{\zeta}_h\|_2}$ and $\hat{w}^{(2)}_h=\sqrt{\|\hat{\zeta}_h\|_2}$ and verify (\ref{eq:kkt-w}).

nodes.name: Proof of GLN-norm closed form for $C=H=2$
nodes.statement: Reduce the minimization over $\zeta\in\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2\times D}$ to a one-parameter convex minimization in $\alpha$ via a parameterization of $\zeta_{11}$, then identify the closed form (\ref{eq:beta-norm-3}) and equate it to (\ref{eq:beta-norm-2}) using equivariance.

nodes.name: Reduce to one-parameter optimization
nodes.statement: Solve the constraint to express $\zeta_{12},\zeta_{21},\zeta_{22}$ in terms of $\zeta_{11}$, then reduce further to a scalar parameter $\alpha=\sqrt{g_1(\zeta_{11})}/g(\zeta_{11})\in[0,1]$.

nodes.name: Solve stationarity in $\alpha$
nodes.statement: Set $\partial\tilde g/\partial\alpha=0$, obtain $\alpha=\|\beta_{11}-\beta_{21}\|_2/(\|\beta_{11}-\beta_{12}\|_2+\|\beta_{11}-\beta_{21}\|_2)$, and substitute back.

nodes.name: Identify both closed forms
nodes.statement: Use the equivariance identity $\beta_{22}-\beta_{21}=\beta_{12}-\beta_{11}$ to convert (\ref{eq:beta-norm-3}) into (\ref{eq:beta-norm-2}).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7 by reduction to exponential loss
nodes.statement: Decompose $-\nabla_{\beta}\mathcal{L}(\beta^{(t)})=-\nabla_{\beta}\tilde{\mathcal{L}}(\beta^{(t)})(1+\delta^{(t)})$ where $\tilde{\mathcal{L}}$ is the exponential-loss surrogate, show $\delta^{(t)}\to 0$ using the tight-tail assumption, then apply Gunasekar et al. Lemma 8.

nodes.name: Decompose loss derivative
nodes.statement: Write $-\ell'(m_n^{(t)})=c\exp(-am_n^{(t)})(1+\delta_n^{(t)})$ where $|\delta_n^{(t)}|$ is squeezed by the tight exponential tail.

nodes.name: Show deviations vanish
nodes.statement: Bound $\delta^{(t)}$ by $\max_n\delta_n^{(t)}$, which goes to zero since margins diverge.

nodes.name: Reduce to exponential case
nodes.statement: Conclude that the normalized exponential-loss gradient also converges to $\hat{z}$, and apply Gunasekar et al. Lemma 8 to yield the support-vector representation.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5 (equivariance over shared contexts)
nodes.statement: Reduce to showing $w^{(1)}_{h\gamma^{(2)}_h}-w^{(1)}_{h\gamma^{(1)}_h}=w^{(1)}_{h\tilde{\gamma}^{(2)}_h}-w^{(1)}_{h\tilde{\gamma}^{(1)}_h}$ for each $h$ and verify by case split on whether $\gamma^{(1)}_h=\gamma^{(2)}_h$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6 (degrees of freedom)
nodes.statement: Construct explicit weights realizing arbitrary $\beta_{\gamma}$ for $\gamma\in\overline{\Gamma}$, then use finite induction over hidden units and Lemma 5 to extend uniquely to all contexts.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7 (norm equivalence in $\zeta$ coordinates)
nodes.statement: Expand $\|\beta\|_2^2$ as a quadratic form in $\zeta$ via the parameterization $\beta_{\gamma}=\sum_h\zeta_{h\gamma_h}$, identify the matrix $M$, and solve $A^2=M$ via the ansatz $A_{\cdot\cdot}=\delta_{dd'}(\alpha+\beta\delta_{hh'}+\gamma\delta_{cc'}+\kappa\delta_{hh'}\delta_{cc'})$.

nodes.name: Two-layer GLN with $H=C=2$ on a 2D input
nodes.statement: An illustrative GLN with two hidden units and two contexts per unit on a 2D input: each hidden unit splits the plane along a coordinate axis, and the four resulting quadrants correspond to four context-dependent linear predictors.

nodes.name: Binary MNIST experiments on GLNs
nodes.statement: GD-GLN, SVM-L2, and SVM-GLN trained on binary MNIST (digits 0-4 vs 5-9) with $H\in\{10,20,50,100\}$ hidden units and $C\in\{2,4\}$ contexts per unit, showing SVM-GLN matches GD-GLN and outperforms SVM-L2.

nodes.name: Binary MNIST experiments on ReLU networks and FReLUs
nodes.statement: GD-ReLU, SVM-RC (random contexts), SVM-LC (learned contexts), SVM-HL (hidden-layer activations) compared on binary MNIST, demonstrating that learnable contexts and the FReLU norm capture much of ReLU networks' inductive bias.

nodes.name: GD-GLN: gradient-descent training of a deep GLN
nodes.statement: Iterative full-batch gradient descent on the cross-entropy loss of a deep gated linear network with fixed (hyperplane-defined) contexts, trained for 3200 PyTorch steps.
input: Hidden units $H$ and contexts per unit $C$

nodes.name: SVM-GLN: convex SVM with GLN norm
nodes.statement: Convex optimization solving $\min\|\beta\|_{\rm GLN}$ s.t. $y^{(n)}\langle\beta_{\gamma^{(n)}},x^{(n)}\rangle\geq 1$, implemented in cvxpy via the ECOS solver.
output: Linear predictors $\beta_{\gamma}$ minimizing the GLN norm subject to architectural constraints

nodes.name: SVM-L2: convex SVM with $L_2$ norm under GLN architectural constraints
nodes.statement: Convex optimization solving $\min\|\beta\|_2$ s.t. the GLN architectural constraints hold and $y^{(n)}\langle\beta_{\gamma^{(n)}},x^{(n)}\rangle\geq 1$, using OSQP.
output: Linear predictors $\beta_{\gamma}$ with minimum $L_2$ norm subject to architectural constraints

nodes.name: SVM-RC / SVM-LC / SVM-HL: convex SVMs for FReLU bias
nodes.statement: Convex SVMs trained with the FReLU group-lasso norm using random contexts (SVM-RC), the contexts learned by GD-ReLU (SVM-LC), or the GD-ReLU's hidden-layer activations (SVM-HL).
input: Context source: random hyperplanes / learned ReLU gates / ReLU hidden activations
output: Linear predictors minimizing $\|\zeta\|_{\rm FReLU}$ subject to the margin constraints

nodes.name: GLN norm encourages sparsity in components $\zeta_h$
nodes.statement: Because $\|\beta\|_{\rm GLN}$ sums $\|\zeta_h\|_2$ rather than $\|\zeta_h\|_2^2$, it acts like a group lasso, encouraging entire components $\zeta_h$ to vanish and thus encouraging predictors to use as few unit-specific context distinctions as needed.

nodes.name: Comparison with Lyu and Nacson et al.
nodes.statement: Lyu et al. (2020) and Nacson et al. (2019) cover broader homogeneous predictor classes but the present approach handles non-homogeneous gated predictors and connects directly to context-dependent linear predictors.

nodes.name: FReLU bias proven analogously
nodes.statement: The same proof strategy used for the two-layer GLN proposition establishes the FReLU bias (\ref{eq:frelu-norm}).
